title: Qualify coherent camera and motion across accepted gameplay updates
trigger: 3D autoplay camera follow direction movement walking stutter flicker fog redraw texture loss view switch GPU resources
guidance: Treat camera direction, walking pose, light and avatar as one coherent presentation of game-owned movement. During Auto, steer toward the current accepted travel direction and advance elapsed-time motion along retained orthogonal legs and the actual stair profile; do not invent a future route or cut through corners. Keep any presentation buffer bounded and reconcile relocation, lost geometry, control handoff and Stop to the committed actor. Repeated stationary/content publications should not restart a step. Preserve unchanged resources through ordinary updates and verify texture restoration and disposal across 3D/2D/3D remounts. Measure frame-time and stopped-motion samples through real cells in addition to unit interpolation checks; an animated-asset experiment also needs an honest viewer-cost assessment.

evidence.reference: codex-thread:01a16a2c-da7b-7042-9108-3dbbc26da0f6; owner stutter/fog redraw, smart Auto camera, steady walking and view-switch texture-loss reports
evidence.note: The requested target is fluid player-like movement and useful camera direction while preserving the working game systems.

Reviewed accepted-neighbor replay, stationary-publication handling, bounded catch-up/reset and shortest-angle steering. This review does not rerun current runtime performance or claim hardware-wide guarantees.

recheck: Reconcile current authoritative movement/Auto scheduling, battle/control fences, stair endpoints and resource ownership. Requalify at changed command cadence and on affected view lifetimes; do not copy a prior queue cap, frame time or speed as a universal guarantee.
